main_text.p: 5. Destinatum. Omnes hominum (tantisper donec sunt ψυχικοί) cogitationes, consilia omnia eo tendunt, ut homo sibi ipsi uiuat, sibi consulat & blandiatur. At qui hoc pugnat cum fine, cuius gratia cō diti sunt homines. Conditi enim & redemti sunt, ut Deum agnoscant, inuocet & celebrent, ut ei uni uiuant, moriantur, resurgant, & in aeternum beatam agant uitam.

Ex ijs omnibus quae [illegible, ~8 letters] licuit, colligimus, Deum merito irridere nostra carnalia consilia, ματαιότητα[?] & conatus inanes & ridiculos: ac nobis eo nomine nefuspecta esse debere omnia carnis nostrae consilia: & orandum, ut non nostra, sed Dei uoluntas fiat. Haec de θεῖα[?] uersus 4.
main_text.head: VERSVS V.

p.i: Egressus est itaq; Ionah ex urbe ipsa, & sedit ad Orientem eius, fecitq; sibi illic tabernaculum, & manfit subter illud in umbra ipsa, donec uideret quid futurum esset urbi ipsi.

page.notes: Greek word after "quae" in the second paragraph is unreadable at this scan resolution. The Greek after "consilia," reads as likely ματαιότητα and the one after "de" as likely θεῖα; both are doubtful. The Greek ψυχικοί is marked doubtful. The top paragraph begins mid-sentence and is treated as a continuation from the previous page. The last line ends with a printed hyphen across a line break. Printed spellings such as "nefuspecta" and "itaq;" are kept as printed.
